materials_read_and_scope: Australian December 2023 inspection report: printed pages 7–9 for logistics, three observers, 12–15 December dates and the 1995 previous Australian inspection; printed pages 29–30 for macerated but otherwise untreated wastewater, the land-first outlet, acknowledged Annex III noncompliance and access/ice difficulties. Plans for treatment are not represented as completed repairs.

Antarctic Treaty text in the official Handbook: Article IV preserves territorial positions; Article VII specifies observers, notification and access. The article does not attribute general enforcement or sentencing powers to inspectors.

Environmental Protocol, especially Articles 13–14 and 18–20: national implementation, reporting and dispute procedures remain distinct. The official ATS explanation identifies the inspection checklists as nonmandatory.

2024 ATCM final report, paragraphs 299–302: logistical assistance and independent reporting are kept distinct; France's follow-up plans are not treated as proof of a completed fix. The older 2012 UK–Netherlands–Spain report supports limited points about snow, communication limits and earlier recommendations not fully implemented.

IAEA GOV/2017/10, paragraphs 7 and 11–12: the 130.1-tonne finding, reported 19 November shipment and 6 December destination verification; 10 January decision, 31 January action and 19 February estimate submission for the 99.9-kg record. Uranium mass and UF6-equivalent inventory units are distinguished; conditional accounting is not presented as a blanket exemption.

UN Security Council Resolution 2231 with JCPOA annexes: estimated heavy-water needs and availability of excess for export; implementation sequence, Joint Commission and dispute process. A measured excess is not portrayed as an automatic agreement-termination trigger.

IAEA GOV/2016/8, paragraphs 5–6: Implementation Day concerned specified preparatory steps. GOV/2018/24, paragraph 27: declared-material non-diversion and the ongoing evaluation of the absence of undeclared activity are different findings.
Trump's 8 May 2018 remarks and the same-day E3 statement are attributed policy positions, not interchangeable with the IAEA's technical conclusions. The historical discussion stops in 2018.

OFAC's 16 January 2016 Implementation Day announcement and the IMF's February 2017 Selected Issues entry/indexed chapter support the limited scope of sanctions relief and continuing banking constraints. Formal relief, private banks' willingness to transact and household welfare are not equated. No present-day legal or investment advice is offered.
